To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

S. indicus, an anti-inflammatory natural product, inhibits the progression of aortic lesion in two animal models of atherosclerosis independent of lipid changes, and the lipid-independent anti- atherogenic effect was associated with the suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokine production via inhibition of the NF- κB pathway.

the anti-inflammatory agent, 7-HF from S. indicus, inhibits the expression of proinflammatory cytokine and adhesion molecules, reduces the progression of atheroma in hyperlipidemia, and does not alter the lipid profiles.

a novel anti-inflammatory compound from S. indicus inhibits the production of inflammatory cytokines and adhesions molecules, which in turn, reduces the atherosclerotic lesion area independent of lipid changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel anti-inflammatory agents for the management of inflammatory diseases, including atherosclerosis.
the identification of natural products and/or their active constituents, which can reduce the risk of atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.
the identification of novel anti-inflammatory agents that can prevent the progression of atherogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methanolic extract and 7-HF of S. indicum are anti-atherogenic, and that the antiatherogenic activity is not driven by lipid lowering activity.
S. indicus is a potent natural anti-atherosclerosis agent.
the anti-inflammatory properties of S. indicis are responsible for attenuating atherosclerosis progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a novel anti-inflammatory agent, 7-HF, isolated from S. indicus, inhibits expression of pro-inflammatory proteins, MCP-1, IL-6, and TNF-α in vitro and in vivo, and slows the progression of aortic lesions in two different animal models of atherosclerosis independent of changes in plasma lipids.
the anti-inflammatory natural product, 7-HF from S. indicus, inhibits the progression of aortic lesions in hyperlipidemia independent of lipid changes.
